rationale: log/tab_ipw_empl.scsv (Table 5 panel B) reports d_t~eusch_pw coefficients per education group. The noncollege nonmanufacturing employment-share coefficient (col 16, d_sh_empl_.. noncollege) is -0.531 with SE (0.203), matching the claim exactly. Summing manufacturing + nonmanufacturing share coefficients within each education group yields the net employment-to-population reductions: college = -0.592 (col 11, d~_mfg_edu_c) + 0.168 (col 12, d~nmfg_edu_c) = -0.424 pp (~-0.42), and noncollege = -0.581 (col 15) + (-0.531) (col 16) = -1.112 pp (~-1.11). All three values fall within ~1% of the paper values, and the noncollege effect is ~2.6x the college effect, consistent with the paper's 'nearly three times as large' description.
